title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Rajeev Kumar
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Stay of PLA award; notice issued; merits not considered
headnote: On a distribution licensee's writ against a Permanent Lok Adalat award in a theft-of-electricity assessment dispute, the Allahabad High Court issued notice, stayed the award, and listed the matter, without deciding whether the Lok Adalat lacked jurisdiction because statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 were available.
facts: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited challenged the 18 May 2018 award of the Permanent Lok Adalat, Moradabad, in a theft-of-electricity assessment dispute. The distribution company said the consumer, Rajeev Kumar, had gone to the Lok Adalat despite statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and that the award was without jurisdiction. Siddharth J. issued notice and stayed the award; later listings by Yashwant Varma J. continued the stay.

holding_units.topic: interlocutory stay of Permanent Lok Adalat theft-assessment award
holding_units.holding: The High Court issued notice on the distribution licensee's challenge to a Permanent Lok Adalat award in a theft-of-electricity assessment dispute, stayed the award pending listing, and did not decide whether the Lok Adalat lacked jurisdiction because statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 were available.

not_decided.point: Whether the Permanent Lok Adalat had jurisdiction to decide a theft-of-electricity assessment dispute when statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 were available
not_decided.note: The Court recorded that the matter requires consideration and granted only an interlocutory stay.
